text:
Objective choice is a plausible explanation for weak rankings, but training margins cannot establish generalization. [gSASRec (2023; IJCAI 2024 summary)](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) identifies overconfidence and instability from sampled BCE and introduces generalized BCE. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.18721) approximates full-softmax training through GPU-efficient selection of informative catalog items. These support testing multi-negative sampled-softmax/listwise CE and gBCE while retaining the SASRec encoder.

Sampling correction needs careful implementation. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025), authors’ repository](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides SASRec variants covering uniform, in-batch, mixed sampling, and original versus revised logQ correction. Corrections should follow the actual sampling distribution; in-batch negatives are popularity-weighted. A [2024 controlled sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent tradeoffs: random sampling favors head items, whereas popularity-based methods can improve balance while lowering aggregate accuracy. Neither harder negatives nor popularity correction guarantees improvement.

Suggested ablation: unchanged SASRec/BCE versus uniform multi-negative CE, corrected mixed-sampling CE, and gBCE, comparing GPU cost and the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Exclude padding, target collisions, and known training-history positives from negatives; unobserved items remain uncertain negatives. [EMM (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0893608026004090) additionally proposes ID exclusion and similarity-window filtering as false-negative safeguards, warranting a separate ablation. Keep held-out labels inaccessible during sampling. Improvements under 99 uniform negatives establish performance for that benchmark; they do not establish full-catalog recommendation quality or explain Electronics/CDs weaknesses without controlled validation.
